To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
joint transmitter and receiver MMSE vector precoding is superior to other precoding schemes in MIMO systems.
the joint transmitter and receiver MMSE vector precoding (Tx-Rx MMSE-VP) with geometric mean decomposition (MMSE-VP-GMD) outperforms the Tx MMSE-VP and the Tx-Rx MMSES-VP with other methods.
the proposed joint Tx-Rx vector precoding with geometric mean decomposition method outperforms other MMSE VP methods in terms of BER performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of joint Tx-Rx precoding and receiver for the MIMO systems.
the joint Tx-RxivMMSEVP design for MIMO channels.
a novel joint Tx and Rx MMSE VP scheme with GMD method and improved scheme, which achieves excellent performance in MIMO systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the joint Tx-Rxcoding is a promising scheme to achieve further performance gain for MIMO systems.
the proposed improved joint Tx-RX VP with GMD outperforms the conventional MMSE VP schemes in terms of BER performance and computational complexity.
the proposed joint Tx-Rx precoding with GMD outperforms all the other VP schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
joint Tx-Rx design is a good choice and GMD is the best specification method.
the joint Tx-RX MMSE VP is superior to other VP schemes.
the joint Tx-Rc MMSE VP is superior to the Tx MMSE Vp, the Tx-Rx MMSC VP and the Tx MMSC VP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we provide a novel joint Tx and Rx VP design for MIMO system with MMSE criterion and GMD method.
the proposed joint Tx-Rx design with GMD is a simple and effective method to achieve better performance in terms of the bit error rate (BER).
joint transmitter and receiver VP is superior to transmitter VP only, and GMD is the most suitable method to specify the joint Tx-RX VP.
